chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about standing at Arafat: is it more preferable to you to be above the mountain or on the ground? He said, 'On the ground.' As for when there is necessity, there is no harm in rising to the mountain.

key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: Necessity/Need (a legal term for a valid excuse or condition)
key_terms.الِارْتِفَاعِ: Rising/Elevating (referring to going up the mountain)
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat (the plain where the main standing of Hajj occurs)

ai.seo_question: Is it better to stand on the mountain or on the ground during Hajj at Arafat?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the preference for standing on the flat ground of Arafat over the mountain is established, reflecting the scholarly consensus that the essence of wuquf is presence in the plain rather than elevation. The allowance for necessity (darurah) accommodates practical constraints like overcrowding, ensuring the ritual remains accessible while maintaining its preferred form. This distinction highlights the Shia emphasis on adhering to the Sunnah of the Prophet and Imams in the physical execution of Hajj rites.
